column1: # json-wide-integers-are-strings and json-integer-token-only). One small unit —
# `Integers`, holding an int32, an int64, a uint64, a ranged int128, a ranged
# int64, a wide fixed-point field and a map keyed by uint64 — read by the engine
#   (1) an integer whose storage is wider than 32 bits — int64, uint64, int128,
#       and a fixed-point kind of 64 or 128 bits — is written as a JSON STRING
#       of decimal digits, and reads as a string OR a number, the same digits;
#   (2) every integer field takes an integer token only — digits with an
#       optional minus, no fraction, no exponent, not -0 — and a wide integer's
#       string holds the same rule inside the string. The value never passes
#       through a double and its range is tested on the exact value.
# Columns, tab-separated: name, root, json file, verdict, what it holds.
